correctness.rationale: For any symmetric perturbation, the worst quadratic form in each sign orthant is a symmetric sign-vertex matrix. For negative correlation, the coherent all-plus vertex dominates and its two explicit eigenvalues prove the exact radius. At zero correlation, the family is diagonal. For positive correlation, each sign vertex splits into a two-dimensional group-constant block and positive orthogonal complements; its exact determinant threshold is minimized by balanced sign sizes. Explicit null vectors prove attainability at equality, and continuous negative determinants exhibit indefinite admissible matrices above it. Algebra yields even/odd condition-number identities and asymptotics. The actual adjacent standalone verifier passed 1,512 exact-rational vertex positivity/negativity checks for 36 rational settings; these are cross-checks, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The explicit sharp all-symmetric-entry robustness radius, its change in optimizing signs between positive and negative correlation, its dimension-parity formula and attaining kernels were not established by the inspected motivating 2026 Q-less QR paper or the inspected 2017 block-correlation article. General interval-vertex and componentwise-singularity theories are acknowledged as prior. Exact evaluation over all sign patterns is the distinction from those general decision criteria. Historical-priority uncertainty persists because some plausible older publisher full texts were inaccessible; their accessible abstracts give no decisive coverage.

Full text of Rump (2003) and Demmel (1992) was unavailable; an older equivalent componentwise-radius example is possible.

The relative-entry interval is a worst-case uncertainty set, not an assertion that actual floating-point Gram computation attains every vertex.

value.rationale: The robust PD radius under independent symmetric entrywise relative error is a natural numerical conditioning invariant for Gram/Cholesky methods. The exact signed-correlation partition transition, attained boundary, and even/odd condition-number calibration quantify a previously unevaluated worst-case phenomenon and give a precise design/benchmark criterion. The result does not claim a new general interval theorem, practical machine error realization or a broad solver convergence guarantee.
